summary: Weekly POC sync focused on throughput: continuous batching enabled + higher concurrency yielded ~2.4x throughput gain but increased tail latency. Agreed next configs (max_concurrency=12, batch_timeout_ms=10, queue_size=500) and soak test. SE to share config and perf sheet.
transcript:
Header:
- Date/Time: 2026-04-08 14:00 PDT
- Duration: 45 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Jared Liu (Acorn), Priya Reddy (Acorn SRE), Emily Carter (Acorn Product)

Auto-generated Summary (may be rough): We reviewed this week's perf runs, tuned continuous batching and concurrency, saw throughput improvements but some tail latency variance; agreed on soak test and config changes.

[00:00:05] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call?
[00:00:10] Jared: Jared here.
[00:00:12] Priya: Priya on SRE.
[00:00:14] Emily: Emily, Product.
[00:00:17] Daniel: Daniel Park from Redwood SE.
[00:00:20] Maya: Cool. Agenda: 1) go over the perf numbers from the last run, 2) tune concurrency/batching, 3) decide soak and next steps.

[00:01:05] Daniel: Quick note — we re-ran with continuous batching enabled and bumped concurrency from 6 to 12, also increased queue_size to 500 for the test. The headline: tokens/sec went from ~1,100 to ~2,700 under steady state. That's about 2.4x.
[00:01:30] Jared: Nice. What's the latency impact?
[00:01:33] Daniel: p50 is still good, p95 moved from 320ms to around 520ms in the worst runs. p99 spiked intermittently to ~1.2s during bursts. There is a small tail.
[00:01:50] Priya: Did you see queuing in the request logs? I mean errors or timeouts?
[00:01:55] Daniel: We saw increased queue wait time but not timeouts at the load we ran. Some backpressure showed up on the worker side — KV cache lookups were more frequent, and we had a couple of slow KV cash hits (transcription: cash vs cache).
[00:02:10] Maya: To be clear, the test used the Redwood Dedicateed pool with the default kernel selection, and quantization profile Q4 was on. Also used prefix caching for repeated prompts — about 60% of requests benefited.
[00:02:25] Emily: Quick question — what's our target latency for production? Stakeholders expect p95 < 700ms ideally.
[00:02:32] Jared: For our interactive flows we'd like p95 < 500ms if possible, but we can accept up to 700ms for some routes.
[00:02:38] Daniel: Given the tradeoffs, we proposed max_concurrency=12, batch_timeout_ms=10 (was 5), and queue_size=500. That keeps throughput high while limiting extreme tail.

[00:03:15] Priya: How does that affect cost? More concurrency means more GPU time per request?
[00:03:20] Maya: Right — there's a cost/latency tradeoff. Batching improves throughput and lowers per-token cost but increases per-request latency for small requests. We'll show per-config cost delta in the perf sheet.

[00:04:05] Daniel: Also wanted to note continuous batching algorithm settings — we tuned the batching window and enabled dynamic kernel reuse. There's a small bug in the local autoscaler that can cause a slow scale-up; not blocking but something to watch.
[00:04:22] Jared: For the soak we should run at 70% of anticipated peak for 2 hours, then step to 110% for 15 minutes. Can you share the exact config to replicate?
[00:04:30] Daniel: Yep, we'll share the exact YAML and the small snippet for the route. We'll post it in the POC repo and send link.

[00:05:10] Maya: I'm going to read some of the numbers from the spreadsheet — rough numbers: baseline (no cont batch, concurrency 6) = 1.1k tokens/s, median latency 210ms, p95 320ms. With cont batch + concurrency 12 = 2.7k tokens/s, median 260ms, p95 520ms, p99 intermittent 1.2s.
[00:05:35] Emily: Interesting median doesn't move much but p95 moves — that suggests tail queuing.
[00:05:40] Daniel: Exactly. The knob we can try is slightly lower batch_timeout_ms (so we don't wait too long) but keep higher concurrency — or add a small fast-fallback model for short prompts.

[00:06:22] Priya: Does Redwood support automatic fallback to a smaller model when queue_length exceeds threshold?
[00:06:26] Maya: Yes, we have routing policies; can route to cheaper model variant or region. We'll need to configure routes and a canary window.
[00:06:35] Jared: For data security — are the audit logs and KMS integration still available on Dedicated? We need SOC two/ISO level audits.
[00:06:40] Maya: Dedicated has KMS/HSM options and we can turn on audit logging; we will send the security pack.

[00:07:15] Daniel: Back to tuning — queueing behavior: with queue_size at 500 we had slow buildup during ramp up but steady state was ok. If customer wants lower tail, set queue_size lower (200) and accept lower throughput.
[00:07:35] Emily: Which is preferable for our product? We have both short single-turn and longer multi-turn writes.
[00:07:40] Jared: We should keep the short-turn route on a route with smaller batch targets and lower concurrency. Long-turn can batch more aggressively.
[00:07:50] Maya: Good pattern — split routes by expected tokens/turns and set per-route concurrency and batching.

[00:08:40] Daniel: Observability note — instrument token-level traces and route-level QPS. We put sample queries in Grafana: 1) per-route latency histogram, 2) batch size distribution, 3) queue wait time percentiles.
[00:09:05] Priya: We'll need those dashboards. Please include example alerts for p95 > 800ms or error rate > 0.5%.
[00:09:12] Daniel: Will do.

[00:10:00] Jared: Did you test with prefix caching on vs off? Because our request patterns have a lot of repeated system prompts.
[00:10:05] Daniel: Yes — prefix cache on gave about 30% lower token cost and reduced latency for cached requests; however cache eviction behavior needs to be tuned for memory limits. Sometimes the cache lookups turned into KV cash slow hits as I said earlier.
[00:10:20] Emily: Are there any gotchas for on-prem / private deploys? We might do Private later.
[00:10:25] Maya: Private has same runtime but different telemetry hooks; also KMS integration depends on your HSM. We'll cover in a separate security call.

[00:11:00] Daniel: Quick demo of the perf plot (screen share transcribed roughly): you can see throughput vs concurrency curve — past concurrency ~14 we see diminishing returns. CPU/GPU utilization tops out and tails get worse. So recommended sweet spot is 10-14 depending on model/seq length.
[00:11:25] Jared: For our mix (avg seq 180 tokens) looks like 12 is a reasonable choice.
[00:11:30] Daniel: Agreed.

[00:12:10] Priya: About autoscaling — can we guarantee scale-up latency under sudden bursts?
[00:12:15] Maya: Scale-up depends on reserved capacity and warm nodes. For Dedicated we can provision burst nodes and have a warm pool; that reduces scale latency but costs more. SE note: warm pool config recommended for production.
[00:12:35] Jared: Ok. Set a test to run with warm pool enabled so we measure realistic behavior.

[00:13:00] Emily: Any security docs we should look at before we proceed?
[00:13:05] Maya: We'll send the security packet (SOC 2, ISO summary, KMS integration guide, and RBAC docs).

[00:13:45] Daniel: Another thing — kernel selection: for longer sequences the runtime picked a different kernel that favors throughput; for short sequences it selected a low-latency kernel. We saw a small mismatch where sequence distribution changed mid-run and caused jitter. Suggest pinning kernel policy per route for consistency.

[00:14:10] Priya: That makes sense. We'll keep route-level pinning for interactive routes.

[00:15:00] Jared: For the soak test please include these scenarios: baseline load at 70% for 2 hours, step to 110% for 15 mins, short-burst scenario with 500 concurrent short requests, and a failure injection where one worker is taken offline.
[00:15:18] Daniel: We'll build the test plan and share it.

[00:16:00] Maya: Recap configs we want to try in the soak: max_concurrency=12, batch_timeout_ms=10, queue_size=500, prefix_cache_ttl=300s for now. We'll also enable batch size histogram collection.
[00:16:15] Emily: Sounds good. Any objections?
[00:16:18] Jared: None.

[00:17:00] Priya: On alerts, add an alert for queue_wait_time p95 > 400ms too.
[00:17:05] Daniel: Will add.

[00:18:00] Maya: I'm going to list the deliverables: 1) perf spreadsheet with run-by-run numbers (Maya), 2) config snippet + gist (Daniel), 3) soak test plan (Daniel), 4) security docs (Maya).
[00:18:15] Emily: Can we get the perf sheet by end of Friday?
[00:18:19] Maya: Yes, I'll send by 2026-04-10.

[00:19:00] Jared: Question — any recommended tokenization changes or batching heuristics for our tokenizer?
[00:19:05] Daniel: Mostly route-level heuristics; smaller requests should be on smaller concurrency and smaller batching windows. We can show heuristics in a doc.

[00:20:00] (brief cross talk about a link sharing glitch)

[00:21:30] Daniel: Posting the gist now (link omitted in transcript). It includes the YAML snippet to set route.concurrency_limit, route.batch_settings.batch_timeout_ms, and queue.max_size.

[00:22:10] Priya: We'll run the soak starting Monday and report back.
[00:22:15] Emily: Timeline wise, after the soak we want a canary to roll in production week of 2026-04-20.

[00:23:00] Jared: A couple more notes — we may want a small model warm-fallback for very short prompts to reduce p95. Daniel, can you propose options and cost delta?
[00:23:05] Daniel: Yes — include 2 options: 1) route fallback to smaller model on queue_threshold, 2) route split where short-turn route uses small model always. I'll include cost estimates.

[00:24:40] Maya: Any blockers we should flag?
[00:24:44] Emily: No blockers. Just need the perf sheet and the config.

[00:25:10] Daniel: One more perf detail — quantization profile Q4 gave lower memory footprint but the kernel for Q4 had higher setup cost which impacted very short requests. If p95 is important for short prompts, try Q8 or different kernel.
[00:25:30] Jared: Noted.

[00:26:20] Priya: Logging — we want request IDs to be passed through; make sure your SDK is instrumented to carry trace IDs.
[00:26:25] Maya: Redwood SDK includes trace_id passthrough by default, we'll confirm.

[00:27:00] (minor discussion about upcoming legal review; not captured in depth)

[00:28:10] Maya: Ok final recap and owners: Maya sends perf sheet (04/10), Daniel shares config + soak plan (04/09), Jared runs soak and sends logs (04/13). After soak we meet to review results.

[00:28:35] Emily: That works. Anything else?
[00:28:40] Jared: Nothing from me.
[00:28:45] Priya: No.

[00:29:00] Maya: Great, thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the links and sheet.
[00:29:05] Daniel: Thanks all.

[00:29:20] (meeting ends early; system notes show call length 30:12 in the cloud recording but calendar blocked 45 minutes)

Notes: transcription imperfect in places — "KV cash" instead of KV cache, "Redwood Dedicateed" mis-transcribed. References to shared artifacts: perf spreadsheet (link to be sent), config gist (link to be sent), security packet (link to be sent).
